verdict: Caution: lend selectively to Rudrapur two-wheeler dealers and aftermarket parts sellers with clean stock-and-cash discipline; avoid sub-dealers and EV-only showrooms until local demand signals improve.
title: Rudrapur two-wheelers: a note to the credit manager
narrative:
## What this business physically is
A Rudrapur two-wheeler borrower is either a dealer/showroom moving OEM stock, or an aftermarket spare-parts and service shop. **Cash turns on footfall and finance penetration, not on the machine itself.** The dealer buys stock from the OEM, funds a working-capital cycle of vehicle inventory plus registration and finance paperwork, and earns a thin margin per unit plus service and accessory income. The aftermarket shop buys parts, holds shelf stock, and collects cash daily. [9][10] say component and dealer channels carry working capital that must be matched by limits; so when a proposal lands, check the inventory days and the OEM credit period before you size the limit.

## Where value and cash sit
**Value sits in the OEM franchise and in the service bay, not in the metal.** Pricing power is weak because the OEM sets the price and the dealer competes on discount and finance schemes; the aftermarket shop has more pricing room but smaller tickets. Capex is modest for a showroom and low for a parts shop. [10] notes that suppliers tied to OEMs get prompt payment while aftermarket sellers carry longer cycles; so if the borrower is an aftermarket shop, ask for the receivables ageing and the actual collection period, collect from customer.

## What has changed now
**The national picture is strong but the local picture is not.** India-wide two-wheeler industry sales grew 27 percent in Q2 [4], and IIP for NIC 30 output rose 25.3% YoY to Aug-2026 [D]. Against that, Uttarakhand GST collections fell 19.1% Apr-to-date versus India +6.1% [D], and state electricity demand grew only 4.7% versus India +9.5% [D]. **Treat Rudrapur demand as softer than the national headline.** Local news is thin on this industry: [2] is a police drive against modified silencers, not a demand signal, and [3] is an e-rickshaw safety protest. So lean on first principles and the peer results.

## Who to pursue, and how to grow safely
**Pursue established multi-brand dealers with service income and aftermarket parts shops with steady cash sales.** Avoid new EV-only showrooms and sub-dealers dependent on one financier. Structure as a cash-flow limit against stock and receivables, with a stock statement and monthly cash-flow statement as conditions. Take every month: stock and ageing, OEM scheme and discount details, and bank statements. [8] flags hedging and competitive intensity; so if the borrower has unhedged forex or heavy discounting, ask for the scheme letter.

## Early-warning signs
- **Stock days rising while sales flat** -> cut limit and ask for ageing.
- **Registration or finance rejection rates climbing** -> reassess borrower.
- **GST turnover falling two quarters running** -> shift to secured lending only.
- **OEM scheme withdrawal or margin cut** -> reprice or exit.
